case: follow-up failure (fault only; no recorded case reaches it)
from: Go commits the ownership-gated UPDATE, then runs the tag rewrite in a second transaction, so a failing rewrite answers 500 with released_at already set
to: rust_mailsec_quarantine_release runs both in one transaction: a failing rewrite answers 500 and leaves the row active
reason: ARCH-028 statement-or-reducer rule: Go's handler is two writes, so Rust calls one reducer. The rewrite (release_quarantine_tags) cannot fail for a row the UPDATE just matched in a consistent database; the same applies to the user and admin reject follow-ups (soft-delete, swallowed hard delete) on the sibling routes.

from: Go hands the report to its in-process trainer queue (no database effect)
to: the reducer emits pg_notify('spam_train', {user_id,message_id,is_spam:true}) in the same transaction
reason: A Rust process cannot reach Go's in-memory queue; the notification is the channel the message_tags trigger already uses, which either trainer subscribes to. The oracle asserts exactly this notification and removes it before comparing with the golden.

from: Go deletes the blocked row and inserts the safe row as two autocommitted statements (a failed insert leaves the delete in place)
to: rust_mailsec_sender_never_block runs both in one transaction
reason: ARCH-028 statement-or-reducer rule: two writes become one reducer. No recorded case reaches the difference (the insert cannot fail for a valid user).

from: Go answers 404 when the ownership lookup fails and 500 when only the audit write fails
to: the reducer reports both as 500 (a lookup error and a missing message stay distinguishable: false is 404)
reason: One reducer holds the lookup and the audit write; a database fault cannot be attributed to one half. No recorded case reaches it.

from: Go commits each of three upserts and then the config_changed notification on its own, so a failing second upsert leaves the first applied and answers 500
to: rust_mailsec_tls_policy_set runs the three upserts and the notification in one transaction: a failure leaves the policy untouched
reason: ARCH-028 statement-or-reducer rule: Go's handler is four statements, so Rust calls one reducer. The upserts cannot fail on a healthy database; no recorded case reaches it.

field: /effects and /audit (system_config tls_* and the tls_config_set row)
from: Go commits the BatchSet upsert, then writes the tls_config_set audit row separately; a failing audit write is logged and the request still answers 204
to: rust_mailsec_tls_config_set upserts and audits in one transaction: a failing audit write rolls the configuration back and answers 500
reason: Statement-or-reducer rule (two writes in Go). audit_write cannot fail for a verified admin on a healthy database; the stricter behaviour never loses an audit row. No recorded case reaches it.

from: Go inserts one row per certificate as separate autocommitted statements, so a failure on a later certificate leaves the earlier rows stored (and sends no notification)
to: rust_mailsec_smime_anchor_import stores every row and sends smime_trust_changed in one transaction: a failure stores nothing
reason: ARCH-028 statement-or-reducer rule: Go's handler is several writes plus a notify. No recorded case reaches the difference (the insert cannot fail for a parsed certificate).

from: Go never repairs a notification lost while its LISTEN connection was down, so a pool built before the outage stays cached
to: the Rust listener clears the trust cache on every (re)connect
reason: A removed trust anchor must never stay trusted because a notification was lost; clearing only forces a rebuild from the table. Not observable in the seed-plus-one-tick oracle.

case: audit message resolution under a tenant-bound request role
from: Go calls link_protect_check_and_audit through the request pool with no tenant GUC; once that pool is RLS-bound the mailbox-scoped message lookup sees no row and message_id stays NULL
to: Rust runs the reducer in a receipted transaction scoped to the signed token's mailbox, so the same lookup resolves the message (the reducer's documented intent)
reason: Identical on the pre-flip pool the goldens are recorded on (message-found and foreign-message cases); under RLS Rust is the one that links the audit row to its message. Ownership is the verified token's mailbox in both.

from: Go reads feature.link_protect_strict_mode from an in-memory cache refreshed by notification
to: Rust reads the feature_toggles row on each click (absent row: registry default ON)
reason: No observable difference except the cache's reload latency. With the Spamhaus scanner alone strict mode can never change a verdict (base verdict is unknown only after a scanner error, and all-errors passthrough beats strict), so the recorded strict-on case is identical either way.

from: Go resolves the scan target with net/url and the Go resolver, and calls the live Google Safe Browsing API when SAFEBROWSING_API_KEY is set
to: Rust ports the net/url authority and escape rules, Go's isDomainName and the DBL rules (hickory resolver), and posts the same Safe Browsing request; the Safe Browsing leg is covered by unit tests against a local server, not a Go recording
reason: The goldens run Go and Rust against the same fake DBL (userinfo decoys, IPv6, bad escapes, bare domains and invalid names are recorded). Go cannot be recorded against Google without network and a key.
